apartments.name: Sebastiana (75 m²)
apartments.description: Traced 1:1 from the SVG floor plan: closed 7-vertex perimeter + 7 interior wall segments, extruded to 3.2 m (real ceiling height). Single uniform scale anchored at drawing depth 544 px = 13.0 m (~2.39 cm/px), origin at outline top-left; width works out to 7.15 m. Room names from source labels with user corrections: 'terrace' = second bedroom, east shaft + middle connector = one L-shaped corridor (main-entrance space), hall + bedroom 2 = one space (bedroom 2), 'study' = bathroom (its corridor-facing corner is chamfered 45°, door on the cut edge). Openings: main entrance door on the west wall (y ≈ 6.58) into the corridor, stone-framed entrance (no door) kitchen↔living room, framed doors bedroom↔living room (y ≈ 10.75), bedroom 2↔corridor (x ≈ 6.24), a balcony door on bedroom 2's slanted exterior wall, and a 2 m open passage inside bedroom 2 (no door/window); double doors (closed) living room↔corridor (x ≈ 5.81); three windows on the south wall, which faces SW Sebastiana Street; walls are cut around all openings. Room areas computed from wall geometry; ground marks: street, balcony, staircase, plus subtle perimeter segment lengths outside the building. Furniture from the Airbnb photos: bedroom bed with headboard on the west wall + SW-corner desk (photo-verified via sebastiana_4), bedroom 2 bed estimated against the east wall (no photo of that room). Exterior length marks are split per room section via exteriorLabels (entrance/corridor/bedroom boundaries); listing says 75 m² but the traced footprint computes to ≈71 m² — real tape measurements pending. Lighting model: daylight enters only through the three south windows and the balcony door (rendered as light sources); the Shelly eye at (3.04, 6.2) watches the windowless corridor, so detected light there means a carried light source.

sensors.label: Shelly Presence Gen4 — Corridor (entrance)
sensors.note: Main-entrance eye, pointed at guests coming in through the front door. The corridor has no windows and no balcony access, so if this sensor reports light there, a person is carrying their own light source — the light it sees is the corridor fixture at (4.57, 6.71) — the ball of light appears there in the 3D view when that happens. While it detects movement, a red pulsing person marker is placed on the layout at its spot (the sensor reports presence, not position within the zone).
